$comment: CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT — read by BOTH renderers. Backend: app/charts/spec.count_rows, asserted by tests/test_charts_spec.py::test_row_count_contract. Frontend (PR #985): the equivalent row-resolution in VegaChart/chart-adapter, which should read THIS FILE rather than re-listing the cases. The two implementations answering differently is not a cosmetic difference: the server uses the count to decide whether a chart is empty (degrade to a table) and whether it is over MAX_ROWS (refuse), while the client uses it to decide whether to inject rows and whether to offer the expand-to-table view. A spec that counts 0 on one side and 3 on the other renders as 'No data.' in a report and as a chart in the browser, from one stored object, with no error on either side.
$commentRule: THE RULE: count every distinct set of rows the renderer receives. Walk the root AND the container keys (layer, concat, hconcat, vconcat, spec) — a layered chart carries its rows per layer with nothing at the root. Resolve a data block three ways: {values: [...]} is inline; {name: 'x'} is a reference into the TOP-LEVEL datasets map; generated sources (sequence, graticule) carry no rows. A named dataset counts ONCE however many layers reference it. An UNREFERENCED datasets entry still counts, because the renderer is handed it either way and this number describes that payload.
$commentWhy: The naive reading — 'rows live at spec.data.values' — is false for the two shapes Phase 1 produces. altair 6.2.2's default data transformer does NOT inline rows: alt.Chart(df).to_dict() emits data:{name:'data-<hash>'} plus a datasets map. And alt.layer(a, b) hangs rows off each layer. Both render fine; a root-only reader calls both of them empty.
$commentScope: These specs exercise row LOCATION, not schema validity — several are deliberately minimal and are not run through validation.

cases.name: root_inline_values
cases.why: The shape our own emitters build.

cases.name: altair_named_dataset
cases.why: What altair.to_dict() actually emits. Root-only readers see zero.

cases.name: layered_rows_per_layer
cases.why: alt.layer(a, b) — nothing at the root at all.

cases.name: layered_root_named_dataset
cases.why: Layers inherit a root reference; the rows are one indirection away.

cases.name: named_dataset_referenced_twice
cases.why: One payload, two references — counted once, not doubled.

cases.name: unreferenced_dataset_still_counts
cases.why: The renderer is handed it regardless; the cap must see it.

cases.name: hconcat_children
cases.why: Containers other than layer carry rows too.

cases.name: facet_child_spec
cases.why: The {facet, spec} form nests its rows under `spec`.

cases.name: root_and_layer_rows_both_count
cases.why: An annotation layer with its own single row, over a real series.

cases.name: empty_inline_values
cases.why: Genuinely empty — the one case that SHOULD degrade to a table.

cases.name: generated_sequence_carries_no_rows
cases.why: sequence/graticule are computed by the renderer, not shipped.

cases.name: dangling_name_reference
cases.why: A name with no datasets entry resolves to nothing rather than raising.

cases.name: non_row_junk_is_not_counted
cases.why: Only objects are rows; scalars in the array are not.
